A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CCR research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, with retained material identifiable despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-classification results in Figure 2, synthetic convergence experiments in Appendix D.1 and Figure 4, and qualitative prediction examples.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds component ablations, hyperparameter studies, embedding-correlation analyses, and baseline prediction examples.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 retain the same constrained refinement, surrogate estimator, hard thresholding, linear classifier, dispersion, and projection procedures. The new experiments investigate existing components rather than introduce a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, CUB-200, ImageNet, Places365, and the same synthetic generative-model settings. The added analyses vary components and hyperparameters within retained coverage.

E2.justification: CLIP-IP-OMP and lf-CBM remain the external comparators. V2 adds variants without dispersion or projection in Figure 6 and includes the frozen-concept baseline in five qualitative comparisons, Figures 24–28, where v1 presented CCR examples alone.

E3.justification: V2 introduces component-removal controls and threshold/radius sweeps, including maximum embedding deviation as a diagnostic. Figure 2 now reports CIFAR-100 and CUB-200 curves through 500 rather than 1,000 iterations, although whether training itself was shortened is unspecified. The main concept-set and explanation-length matching procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's refinement-versus-frozen-baseline comparison, v2 adds before/after dispersion heatmaps, separate dispersion and projection ablations, threshold and radius sensitivity studies, and paired baseline explanation examples. Figures 5–8 and 24–28 substantially expand investigation of component roles, parameter sensitivity, and qualitative behavior.

E5.justification: V1's Figure 2 does not specify repeated runs or report variability. V2 newly reports five runs for CCR and its frozen-concept baseline across all five benchmarks, plotting means with minimum–maximum bands. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting, without establishing an increase over v1's undisclosed run count.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial diagnostic and sensitivity results. Figure 6 shows higher accuracy after removing either component, with longer explanations without dispersion and maximum embedding drift around 0.6 without projection versus 0.1 with it. New Figure 28 correctly predicts a bus interior that CCR misclassifies in retained Figure 23. Figure 2 now presents five-run summaries; Table 1 and the main benchmark rankings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The assumptions, definitions, bounds, convergence guarantees, and Appendix C proofs are mathematically retained. V1's Theorems 2–4 correspond to v2's Theorems 2.6, 3.3, and 3.4; numbering, typesetting, and corrected cross-references do not alter their substance.

C1.justification: The abstract and three principal contributions retain the same necessity bound, conditional accuracy/interpretability guarantees, and empirical accuracy/runtime claims, including the CUB-200 exception. The added introductory overview restates the framework's contribution.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the component-removal results as accuracy versus explanation-length or embedding-drift tradeoffs and uses radius saturation to support choosing 0.1. Its Impact Statement also identifies practical hyperparameter tuning as underexplored. Existing dictionary-rank and concept-set limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Figures 7–8 disclose numerical ranges for the new hyperparameter studies, including radius values from 0 to 0.3 and CIFAR-10 thresholds from 0.10 to 0.16. Existing algorithm pseudocode, code-access information, hardware descriptions, and runtime disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Zhou et al. (2018), Interpretable Basis Decomposition for Visual Explanation, and explains more explicitly why Chattopadhyay et al. (2024) provides the chosen theoretical testbed. Appendix A's substantive positioning is otherwise retained; most citation changes are stylistic.

P1.justification: V2 adds an introductory roadmap and an Impact Statement, inserts ablation and hyperparameter subsections, and renumbers the earlier interpretability appendix from D.3 to D.5. Cross-references are corrected, while most existing prose and the overall scientific narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column preprint layout to a two-column conference layout. Figure 2 is redrawn with uncertainty bands and revised axes, and Figures 5–8 and 24–28 add substantial visual material. Earlier case-study figures are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical substantiation by addressing v1's unreported run variability and missing component and hyperparameter analyses. Figures 2 and 5–8 make the accuracy, explanation-length, and embedding-drift tradeoffs much more assessable. Paired baseline examples improve transparency, although Figure 28 complicates the retained attribution of the bus-interior failure to concept-set inadequacy. This localized interpretive tension does not outweigh the substantial gains in validation.
